t: Sahagún, a missionary who wanted to help friars understand and convert the Aztecs, worked with Nahua elders and former students for decades to record their religion, society, economy and natural world in their own language.
The work has three texts in one, Nahuatl, Spanish and pictures, and its twelve books run from the gods to the conquest of the Aztec Empire told from the point of view of the conquered.

Held in Florence and unknown to most scholars until the late eighteenth century, it was translated into English over thirty years and has been put online in full, and UNESCO inscribed it in its Memory of the World register in 2015.
dyk: Sahagún credited by name the Aztec doctors who dictated the sections on anatomy, disease and medicinal plants; he named more than a dozen of them. The Codex was drawn up by about twenty-two artists, a figure deduced from the different ways they drew eyes, profiles and the proportions of the body.
ev: Sahagún begins the project that becomes the Historia General
The final version of the Florentine Codex is completed
The Council of the Indies suggests teaching the Indigenous peoples in Spanish, and Spanish authorities require Sahagún to hand over his documents
Angelo Maria Bandini publishes a Latin description of the manuscript held in the Laurentian Library
Francisco del Paso y Troncoso receives permission from the Italian government to copy the text and illustrations
The Mexican government publishes a full-colour three-volume facsimile in a limited edition of 2,000
High-resolution scans of all volumes are added to the World Digital Library
UNESCO inscribes Sahagún's work in its Memory of the World register

f.made: Bernardino de Sahagún, a Spanish Franciscan friar, in partnership with Nahua elders and authors who were formerly his students at the Colegio de Santa Cruz de Tlatelolco; the illustrations were drawn by native artists
f.form: A manuscript of 2,500 pages in twelve books, in three bound volumes, with a Nahuatl text, a Spanish text and pictures; the pages are generally in two columns, Nahuatl on the right and Spanish on the left
f.where: Biblioteca Medicea-Laurenziana in Florence, Italy, as Palat. 218-220; earlier drafts survive in Madrid; scans are online at the World Digital Library and in the Getty Research Institute's Digital Florentine Codex
f.known: A record of Aztec religion, society, economics and natural history; Book 12, the conquest told from the side of the conquered of Tenochtitlan-Tlatelolco; Nahuatl interviews with elders; Nahua medicine and plant lore; illustrations by tlacuilo artists; Sahagún's methods as an early form of ethnography
